item.title: Zamfara gov’t suspends campaign after road crash
item.description: The Zamfara government has suspended its scheduled campaign activities in Maru Local Government Area following a road accident that killed 15 APC supporters. The victims died along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route while travelling to Talata Mafara for the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally. The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) confirmed that 15 people died, while 27 others sustained injuries in the crash. The accident occurred at about 12.30 p.m. on Monday near Kisami village, along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route. The government announced the suspension in a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Dantawasa, on Monday in Gusau. Dantawasa said the accident involved APC members travelling from Gummi Local Government Area. “The government expresses its deep sorrow over the unfortunate incident and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families,” he said. He also extended condolences to the Gummi Emirate and the APC family in Zamfara over the loss. The commissioner said the government sympathised with the injured and prayed for their speedy recovery. “In this moment of grief, the Zamfara State Government stands in solidarity with the affected families and all those mourning the loss of their loved ones,” he said. He urged residents to remain calm and offer prayers for the deceased and injured. “May Almighty Allah forgive the souls of the departed, grant them Aljannatul Firdaus, and give their families the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss,” Dantawasa said. item.title: Ebonyi govt approves 933.777 hectares for smart city, dredging of 3.3km Ebonyi River against flooding
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has approved the establishment of a 933.777-hectare of new city called FON Smart City in Abakaliki, alongside the dredging of 3,305.61 metres of the Ebonyi River as part of measures to expand the state capital and mitigate potential flooding. The approvals were granted by the State Executive Council (EXCO), presided over by Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, during its meeting. The Commissioner for Information and State Orientation, Chief Ikeuwa Omebeh ehike briefing journalists on the outcome of the Exco meeting, said the proposed smart city would be developed on an additional 933.777 hectares of land acquired from the former Army land within Abakaliki capital. Omebeh explained that the council had approved the designation of the newly acquired territory and its entire development layout as FON Smart City, Abakaliki. He said the initiative was part of the Nwifuru administration’s strategic urban development agenda aimed at expanding the territorial boundaries of the state capital, attracting private-sector investments and stimulating economic activities. According to him, the proposed smart city has been designed with clearly defined land-use zones to accommodate the state’s growing residential, commercial, institutional and developmental requirements. He listed the components of the master plan to include residential neighbourhoods, institutional zones, commercial districts, a Central Business District, green verges, agricultural and farming zones, community resettlement areas and special provision areas. The commissioner said the carefully structured development framework was intended to create a modern urban environment capable of accommodating future population growth while improving the infrastructural capacity, aesthetics and economic outlook of Abakaliki. He added that the project would open up new investment opportunities, expand economic activities and strengthen Ebonyi State’s position as an emerging investment destination in the South-East. Also, the State Executive Council approved the dredging of approximately 3,305.61 metres (3.3 kilometres) of the Ebonyi River to address potential flooding threats within sections of the proposed smart city. Omebeh said the decision followed the identification of flood-prone areas within the proposed development corridor, necessitating proactive environmental intervention to safeguard the planned urban infrastructure. He explained that the dredging exercise would improve water flow, reduce flooding risks and provide the necessary environmental protection for the sustainable development of the new city. The commissioner stressed that the government’s decision to incorporate flood-control measures into the smart city project underscored its commitment to sustainable urban planning and the protection of public infrastructure against environmental hazards. item.title: Surgeons offer free knee replacements as orthopaedic association begins AGM
item.description: … Over 100 patients receive free treatment in Abuja outreach By Ruth Onyekachi No fewer than 100 people living with disabling bone and joint conditions received free medical attention on Monday as Nigerian orthopaedic surgeons began a three-day surgical outreach in Abuja, offering procedures, including costly knee replacements, to patients who cannot afford them. The outreach, organised by the Nigerian Orthopaedic Association (NOA) as part of activities marking its 49th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Scientific Conference, will run until Wednesday across five hospitals in the Federal Capital Territory. The participating facilities are Wuse District Hospital, Garki Hospital, Federal Medical Centre, Abuja, Cedarcrest Hospital and Alliance Hospital, where orthopaedic surgeons drawn from across the country are providing consultations, surgeries and post-operative care at no cost to beneficiaries. For many of the patients, the intervention represents an opportunity to access procedures that would ordinarily cost millions of naira, particularly knee replacement surgeries that remain beyond the reach of low-income Nigerians. Vice President of the association, Dr Christian Madubueze, who represented its President, Dr E.A. Orimolade, said the outreach was part of NOA’s commitment to making specialised orthopaedic care accessible to underserved Nigerians. “This is not the first time we have done an outreach with the FCT — we did one during our 2023 AGM that was hosted here, and we were very happy, we were well treated, and we were able to serve patients,” he said. He disclosed that the association would undertake a significant number of knee replacement operations free of charge. “We are doing a significant number of knee replacement surgeries which normally would have cost these patients millions of naira, but we as an association are going to do them here,” he explained. Madubueze said the choice of established hospitals was deliberate because complex procedures such as joint replacement require standard operating theatres and specialised facilities. “It is actually not possible for us to be doing this in the villages unless we are going to set up a makeshift hospital there, which will dramatically increase the cost,” he said, adding that “Wuse District Hospital is very important to us.” The FCT administration also welcomed the initiative, describing it as an important intervention for residents who struggle to access specialised medical services. Director of Clinical Services, Dr Osayande Osagie, who represented the Mandate Secretary for Health Services and Environment, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, said the administration appreciated the association for bringing the services closer to the people. “Orthopaedic surgery or consultations are not things that are cheap to find, especially in a town like Abuja,” Osagie said. “This corporate social responsibility that you brought to the people of Abuja, we really appreciate it, and on their behalf I want to say a big

item.title: Nigerian children: Millions still face barriers to education, protection
item.description: …Demand free education, stronger safeguards, greater voice in decisions By Chioma Obinna For millions of Nigerian children, the promise of a safe childhood, quality education and a future shaped by their dreams remains a daily struggle. From access to basic education and healthcare to protection from abuse and poverty, the gap between children’s rights and their lived realities continues to raise concerns about the country’s commitment to its youngest population. The challenge came into focus on Friday as the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government marked the 2026 World Children’s Day, calling for stronger protection of children’s rights and concrete government action to secure their future. At the celebration, held at the UNICEF Lagos Office under the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future,” children demanded free education, greater protection and a stronger voice in decisions affecting their lives. UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, warned that children’s rights were increasingly under threat globally, stressing that governments and other stakeholders must do more to guarantee access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. She noted that recognising children’s rights was not enough if families and communities lacked the resources to make those rights meaningful. Lafoucriere explained that social protection programmes were essential to helping vulnerable children access basic services, particularly education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said. She stressed that UNICEF was working with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to every child, particularly those from vulnerable backgrounds. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” she declared, urging society to recognise that investment in children could not be postponed. Children want more than promises Beyond the concerns raised by development partners and government officials, the celebration provided an opportunity for children to articulate their expectations of those responsible for protecting their rights. The Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Rt. Hon. Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their welfare, insisting that their experiences and opinions must count when policies concerning them are formulated. He said children were often better positioned to explain the challenges they faced, particularly cases of abuse and other threats to their safety. item.title: ESUT remains committed to quality academic standards, VC tells NUC accreditation teams
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—The Vice-Chancellor of the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, on Tuesday , reaffirmed the university’s commitment to sustaining high academic standards, strengthening quality assurance and improving service delivery. Professor Okolie gave the assurance when accreditation teams from the National Universities Commission (NUC), responsible for Civil Engineering and Mechanical and Production Engineering programmes, visited the university to assess the programmes. He commended the NUC for its efforts in upholding academic standards in Nigeria’s tertiary education system, noting that ESUT had prioritised practical training for staff and students to equip them with the skills needed to address challenges within their immediate environment and the country at large. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that the university had signed a partnership agreement with a Qatar-based Information and Communication Technology (ICT) firm, Vertex Labs, to establish a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (AI). He added that representatives of the company were expected to arrive soon to expand the scope of the partnership to include the fabrication of computer accessories. According to him, the initiative builds on the selection of ESUT by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) as a South-East Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Cybersecurity and other related fields. Professor Okolie also disclosed that the university management had inaugurated an ICT Innovation Hub to provide staff and students with practical training and professional certification programmes that would enhance their employability and economic independence after graduation. He emphasised the importance of engineering in driving the university’s innovation agenda, adding that the institution makes adequate preparations for accreditation exercises by setting aside special funds ahead of time. The Vice-Chancellor further acknowledged TETFund’s contributions towards the procurement of equipment required for accreditation exercises and assured the visiting teams of the full support and cooperation of the university management. Speaking at the ESUT Council Chamber, the leader of the Civil Engineering accreditation team, Professor Mohammed Saidu, said the exercise was not intended to witch-hunt the university but to objectively assess its compliance with established academic standards. He assured the university that the teams would discharge their responsibilities with professionalism, objectivity and due diligence. The accreditation team for Mechanical and Production Engineering was led by Professor Aje Tokan of the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University, Bauchi State. item.title: Zero-dose children: Lagos, Kano charged to sustain immunisation gains
item.description: …As GSK-supported Save The Children BOOST project approaches 2027 close-out By Sola Ogundipe Lagos and Kano States have been urged to take full ownership of the Better Opportunities for Optimal Services and Targeted Immunisation for Zero-Dose and Under-Immunised Children (BOOST) programme towards making adequate budgetary provisions to sustain its gains ahead of the project’s expected close-out in 2027. The call came amid continuing efforts to bridge Nigeria’s zero-dose and under-immunisation gaps, with stakeholders warning that local ownership, sustainable financing and stronger primary healthcare delivery will be critical to ensuring that children are not left unprotected when donor-supported interventions end. BOOST is a four-year initiative funded by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) and implemented by Save the Children International (SCI) in Lagos and Kano States. It seeks to reduce the number of children who have never received routine vaccines or have missed important doses in their immunisation schedules. The programme is built around the principle that no child should be left unprotected against vaccine-preventable diseases because of where they live, their family’s economic circumstances or weaknesses in the healthcare system. Stakeholders who made the call in Abuja during the Lessons Learning and Transition Planning Workshop organised by SCI with support from GSK, urged government officials and civil society organisations from both states to review the project’s sustainability prospects, share best practices and develop strategies for transferring successful interventions to government-led interventions. Participants said sustaining improvements in immunisation coverage and reducing the number of zero-dose and under-immunised children would depend on state governments adopting successful project innovations, strengthening partnerships with civil society organisations and maintaining community engagement beyond the programme’s lifespan. The Policy and Advocacy Coordinator of the GSK-supported BOOST Project in Lagos State, Dr Itunu Dave-Agboola, said the programme had recorded significant improvements in immunisation coverage and acceptance across its intervention local government areas. “I would say the project has been successful because, looking at data coming in from the intervention LGAs, there’s a significant improvement in immunisation coverage and acceptance. We have enjoyed effective collaboration from the governments of both states, both at the level of the Ministry of Health and Primary Health Care Board. They have been very supportive and collaborative. We supported them to implement a lot of their activities. “The collaboration is a strong one such that we see sustainability even beyond the life of the BOOST project, because that is the most important thing, sustainability, so that the gains of this project will not be lost in transit,” she said. item.title: Discos’ Band A of sorrow
item.description: By SUNNY IKHIOYA The time for another round of elections is drawing close. The people seem to be unaware of where to hold the government responsible. Politicians are only concerned about personal insults and vain things. But in recent times, they have upped the tempo to begin to talk about petroleum subsidy and palliatives for the common man. One thing that the people have not been sensitive about is the fraudulent manner in which the electricity distribution companies are taking advantage of the government’s inability to monitor their activities properly. The NERC, the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission, is there, invisible to consumers. We have also been informed that some states have established their own regulatory commissions, like Lagos, Enugu and others. They, too, do not seem to be making their presence felt. Just like petrol, electricity is also at the centre of a people’s development. A country that cannot independently generate its own electricity is as good as staying dead at the bottom. Manufacturers cannot produce, skilled and small businesses will not grow, and the people will remain unhappy. Presently, the high-handedness of the electricity distribution companies is a principal cause of the downward drop in our poverty ratings. The middle class has been completely wiped out, businesses are dying, and no one seems to care. You know why our situation is so despicable: the state of Iran has been at war with the US and Israel for close to a year now, with critical infrastructure badly destroyed. In the midst of all these disruptions, it is still able to supply vital electricity to its people and businesses. The same thing is happening to Ukraine against Russia. Without light, the people are finished. It is a basic principle and also has some spiritual undertone. When you have light, you prevail over challenges and adversaries. That is why our situation is so pathetic. And so they came up with the structuring of the billing system, arguing that with a cost-reflective—no subsidy—tariff system in place, the power companies could be motivated to produce satisfactory power supply to the people and businesses. They embarked on classifying consumers into Classes A–D categories. Although this did not go well with the people, because it clearly was discriminatory and assumed to favour only the wealthy class, it has all turned out to be a scam on the consumers in that category. The Discos have used the monopoly they possess to fleece innocent consumers and businesses of their hard-earned income, with many of them finding it difficult to cope. Yet, on a monthly basis, the bills will arrive. In announcing the cost-reflective tariffs, the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission emphasised that Band A customers will enjoy a minimum of 20 hours of uninterrupted power supply in a day. item.title: 2027: Shunning ethnicity and religion
item.description: As Nigerians prepare for next year’s general elections, they must move beyond the unhealthy politics of ethnicity and religion in the campaigns and choice of leaders. While diversity and equitable representation deserve recognition, they must not take precedence over competence, accountability and proven track records of service delivery. Nigeria cannot build a united democracy on religious intolerance, ethnic suspicion and political exclusion. The country’s numerous ethnic nationalities, languages, cultures and religious traditions should be sources of strength. Sadly, politicians and influential interest groups increasingly manipulate these identities to deepen divisions, promote intolerance and weaken national unity. The emerging political atmosphere is reminiscent of the 2023 general elections, when ethnic and religious considerations dominated campaigns and public discourse. The European Union Election Observation Mission (EU-EOM), in its final report, expressed concern over divisive language and the mobilisation of ethnic and religious sentiments during the elections. It is particularly disturbing that candidates are increasingly judged not by their competence, records and policy proposals but by their faith, language or geographical origin. Political differences or disagreements are sinisterly framed as grievances against entire ethnic or religious communities. Such tendencies undermine democratic competition and threaten peaceful coexistence. The Constitution (1999, as amended) provides clear safeguards against this divisive politics. Section 10 prohibits the adoption of any religion as a state religion, while Section 15 promotes national integration and prohibits discrimination based on place of origin, religion, ethnic or linguistic association. Section 42 further guarantees protection against discrimination on these grounds. These provisions must translate into political practice. No Nigerian should be denied the opportunity to aspire to public office because of religious belief or ethnic origin. Equally, political appointments and access to public opportunities must be guided by fairness, merit and competence rather than narrow identity considerations. Religious leaders must also recognise their responsibility to promote peace, tolerance and mutual respect. Pulpits and religious platforms should never become instruments for spreading political hatred or hostility against people of other faiths. Traditional rulers, community leaders and ethnic associations must similarly resist manipulation by partisan interests. Cultural pride should never become an excuse for intolerance. Politicians who exploit religious and ethnic sentiments for electoral advantage must understand that the divisions they create often outlive their political ambitions. The consequences can undermine national cohesion long after elections have ended. item.title: Taxation or imposition: The state, economy and citizenship in Nigeria (2), by Usman Sarki
item.description: “We cannot demand twenty-first-century compliance with twentieth-century communication .” — Mohammed Idris Bultu The first part of this article examined taxation as a relationship between the state and the citizen and ended with a fundamental question: what does the state owe the citizen after collecting his money? Two thoughtful responses to that article have since helped to sharpen the inquiry considerably. Barrister Muhammad Betara, an Abuja-based lawyer, approached the subject mainly from the standpoint of law and public administration, while Mohammed Idris Bultu, a Tax Controller with the Nigeria Revenue Service in Kano, responded from the practical experience of a tax administrator who encounters taxpayers, assessments, compliance and collection in the field. Taken together, their observations provide an important bridge between theory, law and administrative practice. Barrister Betara’s central point is that Nigeria is not without a legal framework for taxation. On the contrary, the Constitution and the recent tax reforms impose clear duties upon citizens and create elaborate machinery for assessment, collection and administration. According to him, Section 24(f) of the 1999 Constitution places upon every citizen the duty to declare his income honestly and pay his tax promptly. That obligation is direct and enforceable. At the same time, the Constitution declares that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government and places upon the state broad responsibilities relating to economic welfare, justice and social order. Betara’s important observation is that an imbalance exists between these two sides of the constitutional bargain. The citizen’s obligation to pay tax is concrete and enforceable, while many of the wider welfare obligations of government cannot be enforced by the citizen in quite the same manner. This immediately raises the problem of reciprocity. If the state possesses machinery to compel compliance from the citizen, what equivalent machinery exists which enables the citizen to compel transparency, accountability and adequate service delivery from the state? This lies very close to the heart of the distinction between taxation and imposition. The recent tax reforms have sought to strengthen and modernise the administrative capacity of government. They aim to harmonise tax administration, rationalise procedures, improve taxpayer identification, expand the tax base and provide mechanisms for objection and appeal. Barrister Betara therefore makes the important point that the Nigerian problem is not simply the absence of laws. The problem is that the machinery of collection often appears stronger, more visible and more immediate than the machinery of public accountability. Tax Officer Mohammed Bultu’s practical observations reinforce this point from another direction. His first proposition is simple but profound: legitimacy makes collection possible. item.title: Saving Enyimba FC from relegation, by Ochereome Nnanna
item.description: This article is not about football per se. It is about Enyimba International Football Club of Aba, Abia State. Before the coming of our phenomenal and algorithmic Governor, Dr Alex C. Otti, to the saddle, Enyimba FC was about the only thing that made us Abians proud of our state. We were like the eagle chained by bad governance for so long that we forgot to fly. Enyimba is the most prestigious and dominant force in Nigerian football. Three football clubs have historically personified the irrepressible, resilient, successful and enterprising spirit for which the Igbo nation is famous all over the world. The Enugu Rangers International served notice that though we lost the Biafra War, we were not a defeated people. However, though the Rangers dominated Nigerian football and the Green Eagles in the 1970s, their Ibadan rivals, IICC Shooting Stars, beat them to the first achievement of winning the African Winners Cup in 1976. The following year, Rangers achieved the same feat, but IICC fans retain the bragging rights of being there first. Later on, the Spartans FC of Owerri, which was formed around the same time as Enyimba in 1976, became Iwuanyanwu Nationale and dominated the so-called “professional” era. The Owerri club was renamed Heartland FC, a name it wore until it was relegated for the fourth time to the Nigeria National League (NNL) on 25th May 2025 under the hand of Governor Hope Uzodimma. Its first relegation took place in 2016. Imo has seemingly ceased to be a notable footballing state despite an abundance of talents. Enyimba FC of Aba is the real “agba baller” of Nigerian football. It is to Nigeria what Real Madrid is to Spain. It also compares only to Liverpool FC in England in terms of comprehensive domestic dominance and continental conquests. Enyimba remains the only Nigerian club to win the CAF Champions League – back-to-back in 2003 and 2004 – with two African Super Cups. This is apart from dominating in the local league and sharing top prizes in the FA Cup series. If there is any one lasting legacy for which Senator Orji Uzor Kalu will be forever remembered, it is the Enyimba CAF Champions League achievements, which happened under his watch as Governor of Abia State. If you check how our mighty Enyimba FC is doing in the 14th week of the current NPFL season, you will be shocked to see it slumbering in the 18th position – topping the relegation zone! That was how Heartland started before it became a regular customer in the second-class NNL. God forbid that Enyimba will suffer this fate. It will be so abominable, a taboo! Experience has shown that once a mighty club tastes relegation, it always goes back for more. Enyimba must NEVER be relegated! It must return to its pride of place – at the top currently occupied by its elder brother, Rangers. In truth, Enyimba has been suffering since 2015 when Dr Okezie Ikpeazu took over as governor. item.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: Tambuwal commends Gov Ododo for granting ADC access to Buhari Square
item.description: Former Sokoto State Governor and African Democratic Congress chieftain, Aminu Tambuwal, has commended Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, for allowing the ADC to hold its rally at Muhammadu Buhari Square in the state. Tambuwal described the gesture as an act of statesmanship, saying political differences should not prevent leaders from respecting democratic rights and promoting peaceful coexistence. In a post on X on Tuesday, he thanked Ododo for granting the opposition party access to the venue, noting that such actions strengthened democracy and encouraged political tolerance. “I wish to express my sincere appreciation to the Governor of Kogi State, His Excellency, for his commendable show of statesmanship in granting the African Democratic Congress (ADC) the use of Muhammadu Buhari Square for its rally in Kogi State,” he said. Tambuwal said the governor’s action demonstrated that disagreements over political affiliations should not undermine the right of citizens and parties to participate in the democratic process. He said democracy was strengthened when political leaders respected the constitutional rights of others to assemble, associate and express their views regardless of party differences. The former governor also praised Kogi residents for their conduct during the rally, commending them for maintaining peace and order throughout the event. Tambuwal urged political leaders to promote tolerance and avoid treating political opponents as adversaries, stressing that disagreements should be settled through the exchange of ideas. “Democracy is not a contest of enemies but a contest of ideas, and that our political differences must never overshadow our shared commitment to the peace, unity and progress of our country,” he said. item.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
item.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. item.title: I have an incurable form of cancer - Farooq Oreagba opens up
item.description: The Managing Director of NG Clearing Limited, Farooq Oreagba, has disclosed that he is living with an incurable form of cancer, saying his treatment is progressing well and he hopes to return to remission next year. The 60-year-old investment banker said he was diagnosed on February 4 following a medical screening but had continued working and maintaining his lifestyle despite the condition. In an interview with TheCable Lifestyle on Monday, Oreagba said he had learnt to manage the illness and remained optimistic about his recovery. “I have an incurable form of cancer. It comes, I treat, and it goes. I was diagnosed in February, after which I rode at Ojude Oba, celebrated my 60th and continued as if nothing was wrong,” he said. Oreagba said he was responding well to treatment and expected to return to remission around March or April 2027. “I am very fine, working as usual and doing what I always do. My treatment is going well, and I expect to be back in remission by March/April next year,” he added. Popularly known as the ‘King of Steeze’, Oreagba became an internet sensation in 2024 after his stylish appearance and horseback display at the Ojude Oba Festival in Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State, attracted widespread attention. However, his battle with cancer dates back to 2014, when he was diagnosed with bone marrow and skin cancer. He underwent a transplant in August of that year and has since continued managing the condition, receiving treatment in Johannesburg, South Africa. Oreagba urged Nigerians to prioritise routine medical examinations, saying his condition was detected early during a screening exercise. He said he undergoes medical checks every three months, adding that people should not wait until they experience symptoms before seeking medical attention. “Early detection saves lives, and I recommend regular checks. I do mine every three months, but even every six months would suffice,” he said. He added, “It is important to know that a cancer diagnosis is not a death sentence. I am making great progress.” The post I have an incurable form of cancer - Farooq Oreagba opens up appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal: Earlier hearing date still being pursued — Lawyer
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The legal team of detained Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, says efforts are still being considered to secure an earlier hearing date for his appeal against conviction, insisting that the January 25, 2027 date is not sacrosanct. Kanu’s Special Counsel, Aloy Ejimakor, disclosed this in a press release on Tuesday, clarifying that the legal team had contemplated moving the appeal forward almost two months ago when the January 25 date was initially communicated to Kanu and his lawyers. Ejimakor said the decision to seek an earlier hearing had remained unchanged, dismissing any impression that the scheduled date was a settled matter. He explained that the Rules of Court allow an appellant to formally apply for an abridgment of time, a procedural mechanism through which a court can be asked to fast-track an appeal and hear it earlier than originally scheduled. According to him, the option remains under active consideration in view of the critical issues involved in the appeal and the urgency attached to it. “Nothing is yet set in stone,” Ejimakor declared, assuring that legal avenues for expediting the hearing remained available and were being carefully weighed to prevent justice from being delayed. The clarification comes amid expectations surrounding Kanu’s appeal, with his legal team signalling its intention to explore available judicial procedures to bring forward the hearing date. Ejimakor, who signed the statement on behalf of Kanu, said the pursuit of an earlier date had been on the table since the original January 25, 2027, date was made known to the defendant and his lawyers. The legal team, however, did not disclose whether an application for abridgment of time had already been formally filed or when such an application might be made. Kanu was sentenced to life imprisonment since November, 2025, and his efforts to appeal the judgment have suffered unnecessary setbacks for one year. item.title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated. The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election. Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State. “When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked. ﻿ Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election. “Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said. Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls. Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric. Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command. “Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said. Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state. However, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership.
